title: Quinoa Crusted Haloumi
subtitle: with Warm Vegetable Salad
description: Just when you thought haloumi couldn't get any better, we've coated it in quinoa, pan-fried it until crunchy golden, and served it with a medley of veggies.

steps.text: Cook quinoa: Rinse the quinoa well in a sieve, then drain. Put in a small saucepan with 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, for 12-15 mins until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for 5 mins.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, bring a small saucepan of water to the boil for the broccoli. Trim the broccoli, then cut into small florets. Thinly slice the onion (see Cooking tip). Cut the capsicum into 1cm chunks, discarding the seeds. Peel the carrot, then shred using a julienne peeler or coarsely grate with a box grater.

Make dressing: Cook the broccoli in the pan of boiling water for 2 mins or until tender. Drain. Put 1 tbs tomato sauce, 1 tbs olive oil, 2 tsp white wine vinegar and ½ tsp dijon mustard in a small bowl, season with salt and pepper and whisk to combine.

Crumb haloumi: Cut the haloumi into 4 slices. Whisk 1 egg in a shallow bowl. Put 1 tbs plain flour and one-quarter of the cooked quinoa in separate shallow bowls. Dust the haloumi with flour, shake off any excess, dip in egg, then coat one flat side in quinoa.

Cook and serve up: Heat 1 tbs olive oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Cook the haloumi for 3-4 mins each side or until golden. Remove pan from the heat. Put the broccoli, vegetables and remaining cooked quinoa in a large bowl, add most of the dressing and toss to combine. Divide the salad and crusted haloumi among bowls, drizzle with the remaining dressing and enjoy.

Did you know?: There aren't many sources of complete protein in the plant world, but quinoa is one of them, making it ideal for those following a vegetarian or vegan diet. Although we cook and treat it like a grain, technically speaking, quinoa is a 'pseudo grain' because it's actually a type of seed.
